description: A Single Mathematics B-style paper with original questions on skew-line geometry, Bernoulli equations, general-period Fourier series, transformations, Jacobians, and probability approximations.
instructions: Show sufficient working to justify each answer.
Answers should be exact unless a numerical approximation is requested.
Begin each main question on a new page when working on paper.
label: Paper 1

questions.stem: Two straight rails are modelled by \(\ell_1\), passing through \(A=(1,0,0)\) with direction \(\mathbf u=(1,2,1)\), and \(\ell_2\), passing through \(B=(0,1,3)\) with direction \(\mathbf v=(2,1,-1)\).
questions.title: Skew Rails and Nearest Separation

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Write vector equations for \(\ell_1\) and \(\ell_2\).
parts.answer: A line is written as a point plus a scalar multiple of a direction vector. Therefore \[\ell_1:\ \mathbf r=(1,0,0)+s(1,2,1),\qquad s\in\mathbb R,\] and \[\ell_2:\ \mathbf r=(0,1,3)+t(2,1,-1),\qquad t\in\mathbb R.\] The parameters \(s\) and \(t\) are independent.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the shortest distance between the two rails.
parts.answer: For skew lines, the shortest distance is \[d=\frac{|(B-A)\cdot(\mathbf u\times\mathbf v)|}{|\mathbf u\times\mathbf v|}.\] Here \[\mathbf u\times\mathbf v=(1,2,1)\times(2,1,-1)=(-3,3,-3),\] so \(|\mathbf u\times\mathbf v|=3\sqrt3\). Also \(B-A=(-1,1,3)\), and \[(B-A)\cdot(\mathbf u\times\mathbf v)=(-1,1,3)\cdot(-3,3,-3)=3+3-9=-3.\] Hence \[d=\frac{3}{3\sqrt3}=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}.\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find a unit vector perpendicular to both rails, and explain its role in part (b).
parts.answer: A vector perpendicular to both rails is \(\mathbf u\times\mathbf v=(-3,3,-3)\). Its magnitude is \(3\sqrt3\), so a unit perpendicular vector is \[\frac{\mathbf u\times\mathbf v}{|\mathbf u\times\mathbf v|}=\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt3},\frac{1}{\sqrt3},-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\right).\] In part (b), the displacement between the two lines is projected onto this common perpendicular direction to get the shortest separation.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Find the volume of the tetrahedron with vertices \(A\), \(A+\mathbf u\), \(B\), and \(B+\mathbf v\).
parts.answer: Use edge vectors from \(A\): \[\mathbf u=(1,2,1),\qquad B-A=(-1,1,3),\qquad B+\mathbf v-A=(1,2,2).\] The scalar triple product is \[\mathbf u\cdot((B-A)\times(B+\mathbf v-A)).\] Since \[(B-A)\times(B+\mathbf v-A)=(-4,5,-3),\] we get \[(1,2,1)\cdot(-4,5,-3)=-4+10-3=3.\] The tetrahedron volume is one sixth of the parallelepiped volume, so \[V=\frac{|3|}{6}=\frac12.\]

questions.stem: Answer the following independent differential-equation questions.
questions.title: Bernoulli Equation and Matrix System

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve the Bernoulli equation \(\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{1}{x}y=xy^2\), for \(x>0\), subject to \(y(1)=1\).
parts.answer: Let \(z=y^{-1}\). Then \(z'=-y^{-2}y'\). From the differential equation, \(y'=xy^2-y/x\), so \[z'=-x+\frac{1}{x}z.\] Therefore \[z'-\frac{1}{x}z=-x.\] The integrating factor is \(\exp\int -1/x\,dx=x^{-1}\). Multiplying by \(x^{-1}\), \[\left(\frac{z}{x}\right)'=-1.\] Hence \(z/x=-x+C\), so \[z=Cx-x^2.\] Since \(y(1)=1\), \(z(1)=1\), and therefore \(C-1=1\), so \(C=2\). Thus \[y(x)=\frac{1}{2x-x^2}.\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Solve \(\mathbf X'=A\mathbf X\), where \(A=\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\2&3\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf X(0)=\binom{1}{0}\).
parts.answer: The characteristic equation is \[(3-\lambda)^2-4=0,\] so \(3-\lambda=\pm2\). The eigenvalues are \(5\) and \(1\). For \(\lambda=5\), an eigenvector is \((1,1)\). For \(\lambda=1\), an eigenvector is \((1,-1)\). Therefore \[\binom{x}{y}=c_1e^{5t}\binom{1}{1}+c_2e^t\binom{1}{-1}.\] The initial condition gives \(c_1+c_2=1\) and \(c_1-c_2=0\), so \(c_1=c_2=1/2\). Hence \[x(t)=\frac12e^{5t}+\frac12e^t,\qquad y(t)=\frac12e^{5t}-\frac12e^t.\]

questions.stem: Let \(f(x)=x\) on \((-3,3)\), extended periodically with period \(6\).
questions.title: General-Period Sine Series

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State the value of \(L\), the period, and which Fourier coefficients vanish by symmetry.
parts.answer: The interval is \((-L,L)=(-3,3)\), so \(L=3\). The period is \(2L=6\). Since \(f(x)=x\) is odd, \(f(-x)=-f(x)\). Therefore the constant and cosine coefficients vanish: \[a_0=0,\qquad a_n=0\quad(n\ge1).\] Only sine terms remain.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the Fourier series of \(f\).
parts.answer: For an odd function on \((-L,L)\), \[b_n=\frac{2}{L}\int_0^L f(x)\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\,dx.\] With \(L=3\), \[b_n=\frac23\int_0^3x\sin\frac{n\pi x}{3}\,dx.\] Put \(k=n\pi/3\). Then \[\int_0^3x\sin kx\,dx=\left[-\frac{x\cos kx}{k}+\frac{\sin kx}{k^2}\right]_0^3=-\frac{3(-1)^n}{n\pi/3}.\] Hence \[b_n=\frac23\left(-\frac{9(-1)^n}{n\pi}\right)=\frac{6(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi}.\] Therefore \[f(x)\sim\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{6(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi}\sin\frac{n\pi x}{3}.\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use Parseval's theorem to evaluate \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}1/n^2\).
parts.answer: For this sine series, Parseval's theorem gives \[\frac{1}{3}\int_{-3}^{3}x^2\,dx=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}b_n^2.\] The left side is \[\frac{1}{3}\cdot2\int_0^3x^2\,dx=\frac{2}{3}\cdot9=6.\] Since \(b_n=6(-1)^{n+1}/(n\pi)\), \[6=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{36}{n^2\pi^2}=\frac{36}{\pi^2}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^2}.\] Therefore \[\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{6}.\]

questions.stem: Let \(F(s,t)=f(x,y)\), where \(x=s+t\) and \(y=s^2-t^2\). Assume \(f\) has continuous second partial derivatives.
questions.title: Mixed Partials and Chain Rule

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find \(F_s\) and \(F_t\).
parts.answer: The coordinate derivatives are \[x_s=1,\qquad x_t=1,\qquad y_s=2s,\qquad y_t=-2t.\] By the chain rule, \[F_s=f_xx_s+f_yy_s=f_x+2sf_y,\] and \[F_t=f_xx_t+f_yy_t=f_x-2tf_y.\] The derivatives of \(f\) are evaluated at \((x,y)=(s+t,s^2-t^2)\).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Show that \(F_{st}=f_{xx}+2(s-t)f_{xy}-4stf_{yy}\).
parts.answer: Differentiate \(F_s=f_x+2sf_y\) with respect to \(t\). For the first term, \[\frac{\partial}{\partial t}f_x=f_{xx}x_t+f_{xy}y_t=f_{xx}-2tf_{xy}.\] For the second term, \(s\) is constant with respect to \(t\), so \[\frac{\partial}{\partial t}(2sf_y)=2s(f_{yx}x_t+f_{yy}y_t)=2s(f_{xy}-2tf_{yy}).\] Adding these terms and using \(f_{xy}=f_{yx}\), \[F_{st}=f_{xx}-2tf_{xy}+2sf_{xy}-4stf_{yy}=f_{xx}+2(s-t)f_{xy}-4stf_{yy}.\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Apply part (b) to \(f(x,y)=x^2+y^2\) at \((s,t)=(1,0)\).
parts.answer: For \(f(x,y)=x^2+y^2\), \[f_{xx}=2,\qquad f_{xy}=0,\qquad f_{yy}=2.\] Substituting into the formula from part (b) gives \[F_{st}=2+2(s-t)\cdot0-4st\cdot2=2-8st.\] At \((s,t)=(1,0)\), \[F_{st}=2-8(1)(0)=2.\]

questions.section: Section E: Critical Points and Vector Calculus
questions.stem: Consider the plane vector field \(\mathbf F=(2xy+y, x^2+x+2y)\).
questions.title: Conservative Work Field

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that \(\mathbf F\) is conservative on \(\mathbb R^2\).
parts.answer: Write \(\mathbf F=(P,Q)\), where \(P=2xy+y\) and \(Q=x^2+x+2y\). On the simply connected plane, equality of the cross partials is sufficient for a conservative field. Here \[P_y=2x+1,\qquad Q_x=2x+1.\] Since \(P_y=Q_x\) everywhere, \(\mathbf F\) is conservative on \(\mathbb R^2\).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find a potential function \(\phi\) such that \(\nabla\phi=\mathbf F\).
parts.answer: We need \(\phi_x=2xy+y\) and \(\phi_y=x^2+x+2y\). Integrating \(\phi_x\) with respect to \(x\), \[\phi=x^2y+xy+g(y).\] Differentiating with respect to \(y\), \[\phi_y=x^2+x+g'(y).\] Comparing with \(x^2+x+2y\), we get \(g'(y)=2y\), so \(g(y)=y^2+C\). Thus one potential is \[\phi(x,y)=x^2y+xy+y^2.\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r\), where \(C\) is any smooth path from \((1,0)\) to \((2,1)\).
parts.answer: Because \(\mathbf F\) is conservative, the integral depends only on the endpoints. Using the potential from part (b), \[\int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r=\phi(2,1)-\phi(1,0).\] Now \[\phi(2,1)=2^2\cdot1+2\cdot1+1^2=7,\] and \[\phi(1,0)=0+0+0=0.\] Therefore \[\int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r=7.\]

questions.section: Section F: Multiple Integrals and Vector Identities
questions.stem: Use the linear change of variables \(u=x+y\), \(v=x-y\). Let \(R\) be the region corresponding to \(0\le u\le2\), \(1\le v\le3\).
questions.title: Jacobian Transformation

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find \(x\) and \(y\) in terms of \(u\) and \(v\), and compute \(\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|\).
parts.answer: Adding and subtracting \(u=x+y\) and \(v=x-y\) gives \[x=\frac{u+v}{2},\qquad y=\frac{u-v}{2}.\] The Jacobian is \[\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}1/2&1/2\\1/2&-1/2\end{vmatrix}=-\frac14-\frac14=-\frac12.\] Therefore the area scale factor is \[\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|=\frac12.\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\iint_R (x^2-y^2)\,dA\).
parts.answer: Since \(x^2-y^2=(x+y)(x-y)=uv\) and \(dA=\frac12\,du\,dv\), \[\iint_R(x^2-y^2)\,dA=\int_0^2\int_1^3 uv\cdot\frac12\,dv\,du.\] This separates as \[\frac12\left(\int_0^2u\,du\right)\left(\int_1^3v\,dv\right).\] Now \(\int_0^2u\,du=2\), and \(\int_1^3v\,dv=4\). Therefore the value is \[\frac12\cdot2\cdot4=4.\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.answer: The rectangle in the \((u,v)\)-plane has area \[(2-0)(3-1)=4.\] Since the area scale factor is \(1/2\), the area of \(R\) in the \((x,y)\)-plane is \[4\cdot\frac12=2.\] Equivalently, \[\iint_R1\,dA=\int_0^2\int_1^3\frac12\,dv\,du=2.\]

questions.stem: A laboratory assigns participants to labelled experiment stations and then monitors defect counts in repeated runs.
questions.title: Experiment Assignment and Defects

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Fourteen labelled participants are assigned to three labelled stations with capacities \(4\), \(4\), and \(6\). How many assignments fill all stations?
parts.answer: Choose \(4\) participants for the first station, then \(4\) of the remaining \(10\) for the second station, and put the remaining \(6\) at the third station. The count is \[\binom{14}{4}\binom{10}{4}=\frac{14!}{4!4!6!}.\] The stations are labelled, so no further division is needed.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Three of the participants are specialists. If all assignments are equally likely, find the probability that all three specialists are assigned to the station with capacity \(6\).
parts.answer: If all three specialists are assigned to the largest station, choose the remaining \(3\) people at that station from the \(11\) non-specialists. Then distribute the remaining \(8\) people between the two labelled stations of capacity \(4\) each. The favourable count is \[\binom{11}{3}\frac{8!}{4!4!}.\] Dividing by the total count from part (a), the probability is \[\frac{\binom{11}{3}8!/(4!4!)}{14!/(4!4!6!)}=\frac{\binom{11}{3}8!6!}{14!}.\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A run has \(Y\sim\operatorname{Bin}(80,0.08)\). Use a normal approximation with continuity correction to estimate \(P(Y\le5)\).
parts.answer: For \(Y\sim\operatorname{Bin}(80,0.08)\), the mean is \[np=80(0.08)=6.4,\] and the variance is \[np(1-p)=80(0.08)(0.92)=5.888.\] The standard deviation is \(\sqrt{5.888}\approx2.426\). With a continuity correction, \[P(Y\le5)\approx P(Y_N<5.5),\] where \(Y_N\sim N(6.4,5.888)\). Therefore \[P(Y\le5)\approx P\left(Z<\frac{5.5-6.4}{2.426}\right)=P(Z<-0.37)\approx0.356.\]

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: In \(40\) independent runs, the output per run has mean \(12\) and variance \(9\). Use the central limit theorem to estimate the probability that the total output exceeds \(500\).
parts.answer: Let \(T\) be the total output over \(40\) runs. Then \[E[T]=40(12)=480,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(T)=40(9)=360.\] Thus the standard deviation is \(\sqrt{360}\approx18.97\). Using a continuity-style threshold of \(500.5\), \[P(T>500)\approx P\left(Z>\frac{500.5-480}{18.97}\right)=P(Z>1.08).\] From standard normal tables this is approximately \(0.140\).
